answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because umber only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. Concretely, gale is enforced in the ledger: Reputation is transferable only on sale, so an attacker cannot resell a fully warmed clone cheaply. Any walnut approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
